title: To the moon! Navigating deep context in legacy code with Augment Agent — Forrest Brazeal, Matt Ball
talk_summary: A vendor demo uses the Apollo guidance computer to show an indexed codebase agent answering legacy-code questions, then iterating against a simulator until tests pass. The transferable parts are retrieval-first orientation, immutable acceptance harnesses, chat-to-test planning, parallel remote agents, and explicit handling of ambiguous conventions.

takeaways.what_they_do: They index the whole repo and use chat to retrieve relevant files and explain unfamiliar legacy code before asking an agent to change it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Augment has indexed this entire codebase. It's able to go look at it.

takeaways.what_they_do: They give the agent a simulator and forbid changing it, then let the agent iterate until the simulator succeeds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run simulator.py until it succeeds. Do not change simulator.py.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use chat mode to state expected behavior, then agent mode to write tests that check that behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have the agent mode write some tests to check that behavior.

takeaways.what_they_do: Remote agents keep running after the laptop closes and can work on independent tasks in parallel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: remote agents are great when you actually want to close the lid on your machine and allow them to continue to run in the background and in parallel.

takeaways.what_they_do: They note the agent can be convinced either way on a semantic convention, so humans must surface the relevant code and decide the invariant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it couldn't decide for itself whether priority level zero was the highest level or lowest level in the system and you could convince it either way.

takeaways.technique: Small modular modernization with regression tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Convert small portions of legacy code modularly and apply the same tests to keep behavior aligned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start converting small portions of the code in modular fashion to the desired language or you know style that you want and apply those same tests
